answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 200 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is published against the juniper challenge, the knoll audit can replay the haven history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A farm of 3300 identities would post 1809 proofs and burn roughly 47 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
